# Stdlib symbols that are not API

Two kinds of runtime symbol are **not** part of the standard library's public interface, and are listed here so that nothing else has to list them. Do not build on anything on this page: it may change or disappear without notice.

**This page is generated** from `stdlib/*.tki` and `src/stdlib/*.c`, and `make check-tki` fails when it drifts.

## Callable, but internal

These are declared in a `.tki` with `"internal": true`: toke source can call them and the compiler checks the call, but they are plumbing that interface generation reached (story 136.54), not API. Each is either a duplicate of a documented function or a piece of another module's implementation.

## Defined, with no interface entry

Every `tk_*` function defined in `src/stdlib/*.c` that no `.tki` export resolves to (story 136.34). None of them can be named from toke under a publishable spelling -- any that could is exported by `scripts/gen_tki.py` -- so this is the runtime's private half, classified by what reaches it:

| Class | Meaning | Symbols |
|---|---|---|
| `emitted` | the compiler emits a call to it by name: a lowering target | 72 |
| `c-internal` | called only from other C in `src/stdlib/` | 157 |
| `alias` | reachable from toke only under a spelling generation will not publish -- a legacy alias of a published name | 9 |
| `c-api` | a documented C entry point: no toke spelling and no caller in `src/`, but a header, doc page or test names it as API (`scripts/stdlib_c_api.txt` cites which) | 28 |
| `dead` | nothing in `src/` calls it, no toke spelling reaches it and it is not a documented C API (a unit test under `test/` may call it); each is acknowledged in `scripts/stdlib_c_api.txt` with the reason | 1 |
| | **total** | **267** |

A `c-api` symbol is kept for C callers -- an embedder, a C unit test, the conformance harness -- and is listed with the file that documents it. A `dead` symbol is finished or half-finished code with no way in: wiring it up is an interface decision, and deleting it is a glue decision. Neither is made by this page.
